artworks.title: Thomas Wentworth, First Earl of Stafford
artworks.description: The image depicts a man shown from the waist up. His facial features include a prominent mustache and short, curly hair. He is wearing a dark suit of armor with a high, white collar visible beneath it. His left hand is extended outward, palm facing up. The background is a lightly textured surface. The artwork appears to be an engraving. A cursive inscription below includes text identifying him as St. Thomas Wentworth, the Earl of Strafford, Lieutenant General, and General Governor of Ireland, dated at the bottom.

artworks.title: Guzman de Alfarache
artworks.description: The engraving depicts the upper body of a man standing with his left hand on his hip. His head is turned slightly to the side, showing a three-quarter view of his face. The man has pronounced facial features with a mustache that curls upward. His hair is shoulder-length and wavy. He wears a large-brimmed hat with a plume, a doublet with decorative buttons, lace-trimmed cuffs, and a cape over one shoulder. The man holds a sword in his other hand. The background has a crosshatch pattern, and beneath the image, there is decorative script and text identifying the figure as "Guzman De Alfarache."

artworks.title: Jeremiah Burroughes, Puritan Divine
artworks.description: The engraving depicts a man from the waist up facing slightly to the right. The man has a mustache curving upwards, a small goatee on his chin, and hair covered by a dark cap. He wears a dark garment with buttons down the front, a white collar, and has his right hand raised to his chest with fingers slightly spread. The background is plain with an oval frame around the portrait. Below the image is text identifying the subject as "Jeremiah Burroughes, Late Minister of the Gospel," and giving credit to the engraver, "R. Gaywood fecit," and the publisher, "sold by P. Stent."

artworks.title: William Camden
artworks.description: The image shows a man seated, dressed in ornate clothing with lions and fleur-de-lis patterns. The man is facing slightly to the right with both hands resting on a surface labeled "Camd. Britamia." He has a mature face with a short beard and mustache, deep-set eyes, and a high forehead. He wears a dark cap on his head and a large, ruffled collar around his neck. The background includes a wall with a small shield and some text to the left side of the image.

artworks.title: Catherine of Braganza
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait showing a bust view of a young woman. She has a rounded face, large eyes, a small mouth, and a gentle expression, with a centered fringe and long, voluminous curls falling over her shoulders. Her hair is adorned with a decorative ribbon on the side. She is wearing a dark dress with a wide, intricately patterned lace collar that extends to her shoulders. In the background, there is an ornate draped curtain, and partially visible behind her left shoulder, there is an embellished crown. The engraving is encased in an oval frame.

artworks.title: Samuel Clarke, Minister
artworks.description: The image shows a man in a half-length portrait, standing with a solemn expression. He has a short beard, mustache, heavy-lidded eyes, high forehead, and wavy dark hair. He wears typical early modern attire with a black cap, dark garment, white collar, and a brooch. The man holds a small book. In the background, there is a column with an insignia, textured lines, and a passage of text in a formal script at the bottom.

artworks.title: Edward Cocker, Arithmetician and Writing Master
artworks.description: The image is a portrait of a man within an oval frame that resembles a wreath. The man is facing slightly to his right with his left hand resting outside the wreath. He has a mustache, curly shoulder-length hair, and wears a garment with a lace-trimmed collar under a dark outer garment. There is a pin or brooch at his neck. Surrounding the portrait are two winged cherubs on columns, both writing or drawing with open books in front of them. Garlands hang from the columns and there is an inscription on a draped cloth below the portrait. Books, a quill, and a simple textured background are also part of the image.

artworks.title: Sir George Croke
artworks.description: The image displays a portrait of a man from the waist up, facing slightly to his left. He has a serious expression, a high forehead, a pointed chin, and short, receding hair that extends to facial hair. The man is wearing a dark cap and a formal outfit with a ruffled collar. One of his hands is holding a folded object. The engraving around him includes Latin text, decorative elements, and what appears to be a family crest with a helmet and crest. In the background, there is an ornate oval frame with the name "Gorgii Croke" and books or scrolls below.

artworks.title: Oliver Cromwell
artworks.description: The image displays a portrait of a man from the chest up. He is posed in a slight three-quarter view with his head turned forward but slightly to his right. He has a serious expression, pronounced cheekbones, and a relatively thin and straight mouth. His hair is wavy and of medium length, extending down to his shoulders. The man is dressed in a formal suit of armor that appears to be of historical significance, with a high, white, pleated collar peeking out above the armor. The background is plain, with a stippled pattern texture. At the lower part of the image, there is an inscription identifying him as Oliver Cromwell, detailing his titles and roles, alongside credits for the artwork.

artworks.title: William Drummond of Hawthornden, Historian and Poet
artworks.description: The image depicts a man from the waist up, slightly facing the viewer with his head turned to his left. He has distinct facial features, including a long nose, pronounced cheekbones, and a small mustache. His hair is styled back and reaches below his ears. The man wears a dark formal outfit with a large white ruff around his neck, intricate designs on his coat, and a draped scarf of a lighter shade. The portrait is in an oval frame with a decorative crest below featuring Latin text "Gloria Reddit Honores" flanked by lion figures. The background is plain.

artworks.title: William Drummond of Hawthornden
artworks.description: The image features an engraving of a man's upper body. He faces forward with a slight head turn. He has a prominent mustache and short, slightly wavy hair with a receding hairline. He wears a dark garment with a large white ruffled collar and a draped sash around his shoulders. The background consists of an intricate cross-hatched pattern framing the man's portrait. Below the portrait, there is a decorative coat of arms with an eagle atop a shield, flanked by two figures and text, including the name "Guilielmus de Hawtho Drummond" and the artist's signature "R. Gaywood fecit."

artworks.title: William Drummond of Hawthornden
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait showing the upper body of a man. The man is depicted in a three-quarter view, facing slightly toward the viewer's left, wearing a robe adorned with a decorative pattern across the shoulder, and a large, ornate lace collar. His facial features include a prominently arched brow, expressive eyes, a thin nose, and a slight mustache. The man has short, neatly combed hair that is slightly receding at the forehead. Below the engraved portrait is a Latin inscription and a coat of arms, flanked by two figures holding up shields with a winged creature atop them. The background consists of a simple shaded oval, placing emphasis on the subject while the area outside of it is left blank.

artworks.title: William Drummond of Hawthornden
artworks.description: The image is an illustration of a man from the chest up. He is facing forward with his head slightly tilted to the right. The man has prominent eyes, a straight nose, pursed lips, a thin mustache, and wavy hair styled upwards and to the side. He is wearing a large ruff collar with lace details typical of the time. The man's attire is textured, suggesting a patterned fabric. The background includes an oval frame with the name "WILLIAM DRUMMOND" and his birth and death dates. Outside the oval are geometric patterns and a textured background.

artworks.title: Jean Louis Guez, Sieur de Balzac
artworks.description: The image depicts an upper body portrait of a man. He has an oval face with a prominent nose, high cheekbones, and facial hair. His curly hair falls to just below his ears. He wears a period garment with a doublet, buttons down the front, and a wide collar with pointed tips. The background is plain with an oval outline framing the upper part of the image. Below the oval is the inscription "Monsieur de Balzac." The illustration is in a traditional engraving style on a textured paper background.

artworks.title: Princess Elizabeth, Second Daughter of Charles I
artworks.description: This image shows a portrait of a woman, depicted from the waist up. She is positioned to face forward, with her head turned slightly to her left. Her facial features include an oval face with arched eyebrows, large eyes, and a small, closed mouth. She has long, curly hair that falls around her shoulders. Her attire consists of a dark, richly textured gown with a wide, rounded neckline and voluminous sleeves. Around her neck is a necklace made of pearls. The portrait is ornately framed with elaborate, decorative elements like leaves and scrolls. Behind her, there is a cherub with wings, shown leaning over the top of the frame, draped in fabric. The background is filled with horizontal lines. The bottom of the image contains inscriptions in an elegant script.

artworks.title: William Leybourn, Mathematician
artworks.description: The image features a portrait focused on the upper body of a man. He is shown in a three-quarter view, facing slightly to the left. The man has medium-length curly hair, a high forehead, arched eyebrows, large eyes, a straight nose, and a subtly downturned mouth with a small mustache. He is wearing a dark coat with a large, turned-up white collar adorned with tassel-like decorative elements. The background has an engraved texture depicting clouds in the sky and rocky formations on the right side.

artworks.title: Nicholas Claude Fabri de Peireso, French Antiquary
artworks.description: The image is a black and white portrait of a man showing his upper body, including his head, shoulders, and part of his chest. The man is positioned slightly turned to his right, facing the viewer. He has a beard and mustache, with hair that is combed back and appears wavy. The expression on his face is neutral. He is wearing clothing typical of the era, consisting of a loose-fitting garment with a large, plain white collar. There are no visible objects or jewelry on his person. The background of the portrait features a simple lined texture. At the bottom of the portrait, there is text that reads, "NICOLAVS CLAVDIVS FABRICIVS DE PEIRESO SENATOR AQVENSIS" and a smaller inscription, "R. Gaywood fecit Lond 1656."

artworks.title: John Playford, Musician and Music Publisher
artworks.description: The image shows a man standing from the waist up, looking at the viewer. He has long wavy hair, a mustache, and is wearing period clothing with a prominent collar. He is holding a book with music notation and the text "Non nobis Domine" in his right hand. The background features a woven pattern surrounding him and two cherubs at the top holding a musical score with the words "Cantate Domino Canticum nov." There is an engraving below him with text, his age "Ætatis Sue 40," and the year "An: Dom: 1665."

artworks.title: Mary, Queen of Scots
artworks.description: The image shows a three-quarter view of Mary Stuart, Queen of Scotland. She is standing upright, facing forward with her arms crossed in front of her, clasping a crucifix against her chest. Her expression is calm, and her eyes are directed towards the viewer. She has distinctive facial features with arched eyebrows and a small, slightly upturned mouth. Her hair is styled beneath a decorative cap, topped with a crown that signifies her royal status. She is dressed in a dark, voluminous gown with elaborate lace ruffles around her neck, and a large cloak drapes over her shoulders. A chain with a cross is visible around her neck. The background is plain with horizontal lines, and the text "Mary Stuart Queen of Scotland" is inscribed at the bottom of the image.

artworks.title: Cuthbert Sydenham
artworks.description: The image shows a man with a long, oval-shaped face looking at the viewer. He is holding a closed book in front of his torso. He has wavy hair and is dressed in a dark coat with a white collar and a visible vest or shirt underneath. The background consists of vertical lines. There are inscriptions below the portrait.

artworks.title: Lady Eleanor Temple, Wife of Sir Peter Templeof Stanton Bury
artworks.description: The image displays a portrait of a woman visible from the waist up. She faces forward with a serene expression, has long curly hair, and wears an elegant draped garment. She is adorned with a beaded necklace, a strand of pearls in her hair, and a decorative brooch. The portrait includes an inscription identifying her as "The Lady Eli Temple" and contains additional text praising her. A textured background with a coat of arms in the upper left corner complements the formal and historical nature of the portrait.

artworks.title: Barbara Van Beck, the Bearded Lady
artworks.description: The image depicts a person from the waist up in a standing position. The individual has a long beard, a high forehead, and hair pulled back. They are wearing elaborate clothing with voluminous sleeves. The person's head is slightly turned, one hand rests on nearby pipes, and the other hand is by their side. The background features a crosshatched pattern. Textual descriptions are visible in the lower part of the image.

artworks.title: John Trapp, Vicar of Weston-on-Avon, BiblicalCommentator
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait of a man seated at a table. He is facing slightly left and has one hand on an open book and the other hand holding a pen. The man has a mustache, a small goatee, and short hair under a cap. He is wearing a buttoned tunic with a large white collar and white cuffs. The background has an oval pattern. There is a poem or text, a signature, and the engraving date of 1654 at the bottom of the engraving.

artworks.title: Henry Somerset, Earl of Worcester, First Dukeof Beaufort
artworks.description: The image displays a portrait of an individual. The person is facing forward with a slight turn to the left side, looking directly at the viewer. He has long, wavy hair, a mustache, and a slight goatee. The person is dressed in formal attire with a lace collar, a dark garment, and material over his shoulders. The background is plain with light lines, enclosed in an oval frame, and the name "Henery Somerset Earle of Worcester etc." is inscribed at the bottom.
